history: Chocolat reached French from Mexico, by way of Spain. Spanish writers wrote chocollatl around 1580 and chocolate in 1590, from a Nahuatl word. What that word was made of is hard to say: the TLFi calls it difficult to analyse, and only the ending -atl, ‘water’, is identified with confidence. That fits the first chocolate, which was a drink. French follows the same order. In 1598 a French translation of a Spanish book on the Americas describes chocolate as a drink made with cacao beans, and in 1659 royal letters issued at Toulouse use chocolat for a food made of cacao and sugar. French dropped the final e, so today it is le chocolat, and un chocolat chaud is what you order on a cold day.
historyEinfach: Chocolat comes from Mexico. The word is from Nahuatl, a language of Mexico, and it came to French through Spanish. The end of the word, -atl, meant ‘water’: the first chocolate was a drink. Experts don't agree about the first part. Today you can order un chocolat chaud.

elsewhere.text: Spanish brought the word from Mexico to Europe. French first kept the Spanish form, chocolate, then dropped the e.
